Report Description***UPDATE TO REPORT NUMBER 1259548*** UPDATED INFORMATION IS THAT PREPARING CASING FOR CAP AND FLARE OF BLOW OUT WELL. ONE WELL CAPPED AND DIVERTED TO FLARE. TWO WELLS KILLED. OVERFLOW RATE OF 200 MMCF STAYS THE SAME. ESTIMATED REPORTABLE QUANTITY OF 6514 POUNDS NITROGEN DIOXIDE OVER 24 HOUR PERIOD REMAINS UNCHANGED. ***UPDATE TO REPORT 1258415*** THIS IS AN ONGOING INCIDENT. CALLER STATES THAT 6514 POUNDS WERE RELEASE OVER THE LAST 24 HOURS. TWO WELLS KILLED, ONE WELL WAS CAPPED AND IS FLARING, AND ONE WELL IS BLOWING OUT, NOT ON FIRE. THE TOTAL DAILY FLOW RATE REMAINS UNCHANGED. A RELIEF WELL IS PLANNED TO BE DRILLED, AND OPERATIONS ARE ONGOING. AIR MONITORING IS CONTINUING PREVIOUSLY UPDATED INFO: CALLER STATED THE RQ RELEASE OF NITROGEN DIOXIDE IS AT ZERO PERIODICALLY. WELL MIGHT BE REIGNITED MANUALLY FOR SAFETY AT NIGHT, BUT THEY ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY LIGHTING THEM. ALL WELLHEADS HAVE BEEN CUTOFF AND REMOVED THEREBY IMPROVING EFFICIENCY AND ABATEMENT EFFORTS. PREVIOUS REPORTS: UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1258167: CALLER STATED DEBRIS REMOVAL IS IN PROGRESS. WELLHEAD INTERVENTION IS IN PROGRESS AS WELL. THE RELEASE OF THE NITROGEN DIOXIDE IS STILL WITHIN THE REPORTABLE LEVELS BUT LESS THAN THE 13028 POUNDS LISTED IN THE PRIOR REPORT. UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1257297: THERE ARE FOUR WELLS INVOLVED IN THIS INCIDENT. THE TWO INITIAL WELLS THAT BLEW OUT ARE STILL PARTIALLY FLAMING. TWO OLDER WELLS ARE STILL ON FIRE. CALLER STATED A RELEASE OF NITROGEN DIOXIDE WITH THIS INCIDENT. ORIGINAL REPORT IS BELOW: CALLER IS REPORTING A NATURAL GAS WELL FIRE DUE TO A FAILURE IN FLOW BACK EQUIPMENT. FIRE IS ONGOING, AIR MONITORING PLAN HAS BEEN ACTIVATED. ESTIMATED RATE OF RELEASE IS 200 MMCF A DAY.

Report DescriptionTHE CALLER REPORTS A HYDRAULIC OIL SPILL OF UNKNOWN QUANTITY TO THE RICHELIEU RIVER, WHICH OCCURRED ON JUNE 21 AT 11:15AM. THE SPILL WAS CAUSED BY HIGH PRESSURE IN THE DRILLING SITE, WHICH MADE A MIXTURE OF DRILLING WATER AND HYDRAULIC OIL SPRAY OUT OF THE PERIMETER, DIRECTLY TO THE RIVER WATERS. THE INCIDENT HAVING HAPPENED WHERE THE WORKERS COULD SEE IT, THEY IMMEDIATELY REACTED TO DEPLOY ABSORBING PADS AROUND THE BARGE TO KEEP THE PRODUCT CLOSE TO IT, AND, ONCE EVERYTHING THAT CAN HAS BEEN PICKED UP BY THE PADS, IF THERE ARE SMALL PORTIONS OF SHEEN LEFT OVER ON THE WATER, THEY WILL USE SOAP TO GATHER UP WHAT IS LEFT AND COMPLETE THE CLEANUP. THE MUNICIPALITY OF LACOLLE AS WELL AS THE MELCC HAVE BEEN NOTIFIED.

THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY AFTER FIRST APPEARING ON THE WATER. UPON INSPECTION, IT WAS DETERMINED THE SOURCE MAY BE AN INTERMITTENT SEEP OF LIGHT NON AQUEOUS PHASE LIQUID (LNAPL) GLOBULES RESULTING FROM HISTORIC OPERATIONS AT THE FACILITY. THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY AFTER FIRST APPEARING ON THE WATER.
